Crestfallen

KREST-fah-len · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Crestfallen is sad and disappointed, especially after a failure or letdown.

The team walked off the field crestfallen, having lost the championship game in the final seconds.

Worked Example

Crestfallen after her science fair project was disqualified for a technicality, Priya stared at the empty display table where her volcano model had stood minutes before.

Crestfallen describes the deflated feeling right after hopes are dashed -- a specific moment of letdown, not a general mood.

Antonyms

How Strong Is It? — disappointed → crestfallen → devastated

disappointed vs. crestfallen

disappointed vs. crestfallen: Getting the wrong flavor of ice cream is disappointing, but forgotten in five minutes.

devastated vs. crestfallen

devastated vs. crestfallen: Losing a life-changing opportunity can leave someone devastated for a long time, far beyond crestfallen.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — crest

root — crest: the top ridge of something, or a bird's showy head plume (Old French creste)

root — fallen

root — fallen: dropped down (Old English feallan)

Put it together

Put it together: Crestfallen combines crest (the raised comb on a rooster's head) with fallen -- the image of a proud rooster's crest drooping in defeat, now describing anyone whose hopes have just been dashed.

Word Choice

Crestfallen almost always follows a specific dashed hope -- a lost game, a rejected application, a canceled trip -- rather than describing an ongoing mood.
